title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: G is a profinite group (discrete groups are allowed equally) with two chosen elements rho, sigma (1). The left margin says that, in other notation, rho and sigma are the loops l'_0 and l'_1, with rho^{-1}... = l'_infty and a relation of the form l'_infty l'_1 l'_0 = 1. So the model is the fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,infty} with its inertia generators. The marginal title is 'Les groupes M_{rho,sigma} etc'. Grothendieck says he is forgetting the earlier data (script-G, phi) for the moment.

(2) Put eps_0 = sigma^{-1} rho and eps_1 = rho sigma^{-1}. Writing g(x) for gxg^{-1}, one has eps_1 = sigma(eps_0) = rho(eps_0). Check: sigma (sigma^{-1} rho) sigma^{-1} = rho sigma^{-1}, and rho (sigma^{-1} rho) rho^{-1} = rho sigma^{-1}.

(3) L_0 and L_1 are the procyclic closed subgroups generated by eps_0 and eps_1. Hence L_1 = rho(L_0) = sigma(L_0).

(4)-(5) Define the map Phi = (xi, eta) from Aut(G) to G x G by xi(u) = u(rho) rho^{-1} and eta(u) = u(sigma) sigma^{-1}. These are commutators [u, rho] and [u, sigma] computed in the holomorph G x| Aut(G). The map is a 1-cocycle (crossed homomorphism): xi(uv) = u(xi(v)) xi(u).

(6) Three translations follow.
- u preserves the conjugacy class of rho iff xi = alpha rho(alpha)^{-1} for some alpha in G.
- u preserves the conjugacy class of sigma iff eta = beta sigma(beta)^{-1} for some beta in G.
- u normalises L_0 iff eta^{-1} xi lies in L_1, i.e. xi = eta eps_1^nu with nu in Z-hat.

Check of the third: u(eps_0) = sigma^{-1} eta^{-1} xi rho = sigma^{-1}(eta^{-1} xi) sigma * eps_0. Since sigma^{-1} L_1 sigma = L_0 and sigma^{-1} eps_1 sigma = eps_0, the condition gives u(eps_0) = eps_0^{1+nu}.

The next page continues the construction. B_{rho,sigma} is the subgroup of Aut(G) cut out by (6), and Sigma_{rho,sigma} is the corresponding subset of G x G. Under hypotheses (a) rho, sigma topologically generate G (so Phi is injective) and (b) B maps onto Sigma, the group law of B is transported to Sigma. That law is the twisted product xi'' = u(xi') xi, formally the composition law of GT-type pairs (lambda, f).

Purpose: an axiomatic, group-agnostic framework for groups of 'inertia-preserving' automorphisms of a two-generated group with three distinguished inertia subgroups. This is the abstract skeleton behind the Grothendieck–Teichmüller / Ihara-type groups. The next page's margin notes that hypothesis (b) holds for SL(2,Z).
errors: Third equivalence of (6): eta^{-1} xi in L_1 is equivalent to u(L_0) being contained in L_0 (u(eps_0) = eps_0^{1+nu}), not to u normalising L_0. Equality u(L_0) = L_0 additionally requires 1+nu to be a unit of Z-hat (or 1+nu = ±1 in the discrete case). This is a minor gap.
The exponent nu is in Z-hat on this page but in Z on the next page. This reflects the hesitation between the discrete and profinite contexts, not a real error.

ideas.what: Encode automorphisms of a two-generated group by the pair (u(rho) rho^{-1}, u(sigma) sigma^{-1}), a crossed homomorphism into G x G, injective when rho, sigma generate
ideas.modern_name: Parametrisation of automorphisms of F_2-hat by pairs/cocycles, as in Drinfeld–Ihara GT pairs (lambda, f)
ideas.where_published: Implicit in the Esquisse d'un programme discussion of Gal(Q-bar/Q) acting on pi_1(P^1-{0,1,infty}); not in this explicit form

ideas.what: Characterising automorphisms preserving the conjugacy classes of two inertia generators and normalising the third inertia subgroup: xi = alpha rho(alpha)^{-1}, eta = beta sigma(beta)^{-1}, eta^{-1} xi in L_1
ideas.modern_name: Inertia-preserving (special) outer automorphisms; Out^# of F_2-hat; GT-type conditions

ideas.what: Abstract hypothesis (generation + surjectivity of B_{rho,sigma} onto Sigma_{rho,sigma}) defining groups M_{rho,sigma} for arbitrary (G, rho, sigma), discrete or profinite, with SL(2,Z) noted as satisfying it
ideas.modern_name: GT-like groups attached to general two-generated (triangle/orbifold) groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure (cf. later GT variants for other moduli or orbifold groups by Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura and others)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up an axiomatic class of triples (G, rho, sigma) for which the inertia-preserving automorphism group is in bijection with the explicit cocycle set Sigma_{rho,sigma}. He uses this to define groups M_{rho,sigma} and works independently of the specific group, with the remark on the following page that SL(2,Z) satisfies the axiom. A systematic study of which two-generated groups (triangle groups, SL(2,Z), PSL(2,Z), finite quotients) satisfy hypothesis (b) does not seem to be in the literature in this form.
missed.quote: on oubliant (au moins pour le moment) G, phi etc. Soit G un groupe ... On se donne (1) rho, sigma in G
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This gives an axiomatic definition of GT-type groups beyond the free profinite group F_2-hat, relevant to GT actions on dessins and modular/triangle groups. It is modest unless later pages develop it.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is routine group-theoretic setup: a cocycle parametrisation of automorphisms and translation of inertia conditions, standard in the later GT literature. The only mildly notable point is the deliberately abstract framing (arbitrary G, discrete or profinite) aimed at GT-like groups. That framing is likely pre-Drinfeld if the notes date from the early 1980s, but this page itself contains nothing deep.
transcription_corrections: The second displayed system is labelled (6) in the manuscript, not (5); the next page refers to 'les trois conditions (6)'.
The line defining eps_0 and eps_1 is equation (2); its label is not shown in the transcription.
The archive page number on the image is 501; the transcription header omits Grothendieck's own page number, presumably 553bis or similar between 553 and 554 (unsure).
Third equivalence: 'xi = eta eps_1^nu avec nu in Z-hat convenable' matches the image. Also note that eta^{-1} xi in L_1 strictly corresponds to u(L_0) being contained in L_0.
